scenarios.name: VIP Movement — Base Case (Nabanna to Kolkata Airport)
scenarios.description: SIMULATED BASE CASE. A Z+ protected movement from Nabanna, the state secretariat on the Howrah side, to Kolkata Airport on a Monday afternoon: across the Hooghly on Vidyasagar Setu, along the AJC Bose Road flyover to Park Circus, over the Maa Flyover to Science City, north on EM Bypass past Chingrighata and Salt Lake Stadium to Ultadanga, then up VIP Road past Lake Town, Kestopur and Baguiati to the airport and its approach road to the terminal forecourt. Maximum-protocol closure (180 s advance, full closure), default event rates, no weather — the reference movement every other scenario generalises. One planted cause (the profile): a goods vehicle stalls on EM Bypass ten minutes in. Public-safety logistics only: no person is named or tracked. The convoy speed (60 km/h) and the timings are modelled assumptions; the AI proposes the plan and a named officer decides.

scenarios.name: Durga Puja Night — Pandal Crowds and Ambulance Access
scenarios.description: FLAGSHIP. 21:30 on Maha Ashtami (30 Sep 2025, between Saptami and Navami), the busiest stretch of a Puja night. In the North Kolkata belt pandal-hoppers spill off the footpaths around Kumartuli Park and Bagbazar Sarbojanin, along Bidhan Sarani (Hatibagan), around College Square and Santosh Mitra Square; in the South belt the crowd around Deshapriya Park and Ekdalia Evergreen fills Rash Behari Avenue towards Gariahat. Goods vehicles are kept off the pandal belts for the night (the restriction is modelled as fewer heavy-vehicle breakdowns, breakdown x0.6) and food stalls load the kerbs (market x2.0). Ten minutes in, an ambulance (108) on an emergency call asks for a green corridor from the riverside north of Howrah Bridge up Strand Bank Road past Kumartuli, along Bagbazar Street to Shyambazar and down Bidhan Sarani to Kolkata Medical College. Closure policy signal_hold at 45 s: the crowd is regulated, not stopped. Two Kolkata Traffic Police beats and the ambulance are animated (EMULATED units). Crowd loads and speeds are modelled assumptions; the AI proposes each hold and a named officer decides.

scenarios.name: Cloudburst at High Tide — Waterlogging, Pumps and Live-Wire Hazard
scenarios.description: SIMULATED. A monsoon evening (a scenario date, not a forecast): a cloudburst-class cell (rain modelled at 100 mm/h) breaks over North and Central Kolkata at 17:30 while the Hooghly is at high water (MODELLED tide phase). With the outfall gates shut against the river the drains cannot empty by gravity and KMC's pumping stations carry the whole load (pump capacity modelled), so the water spreads instead of draining: Thanthania on Bidhan Sarani first, then the Ultadanga approaches, MG Road by College Street, APC Road at Maniktala, AJC Bose Road at Moulali and Park Circus. A car stalls in standing water; signals at Ultadanga go dark (a modelled precautionary power cut). Where water stands around street-light poles and overhead lines the risk is electrocution: the stack may PROPOSE a live-wire hazard advisory to the power utility (CESC / WBSEDCL) — a proposal a named duty officer approves or rejects; nothing is sent by itself. An ambulance (108) from Lake Town to Kolkata Medical College needs windows through the water. Rain rate, tide, pump capacity and spread times are modelled assumptions, not measurements.

scenarios.name: Cyclone Recovery — Tree-Falls on Arterials, Staged Reopening
scenarios.description: SIMULATED. The morning after a severe cyclone has crossed the coast and passed over Kolkata (a scenario, not a forecast). Squalls linger (STORM, modelled). Uprooted trees block the arterials south from Esplanade: Jawaharlal Nehru Road along the Maidan, Ashutosh Mukherjee Road and SP Mukherjee Road, with Red Road and Queensway closed alongside. KMC and fire-service crews clear them lane by lane, so the corridor reopens in stages (each blockage is a lane-loss cause with its own clearance time). Signals at Exide are dark after the overnight power cut. An ambulance (108) heads for SSKM Hospital through the cleared lanes. Clearance times are modelled assumptions; every reopening is an officer's decision.

scenarios.name: Burrabazar Market Fire — Fire-Tender Access and Ambulance Window
scenarios.description: SIMULATED. A weekday afternoon in Burrabazar (Wednesday 18 Nov 2026, 14:40; a scenario date, not a record): a fire breaks out in a market building in the narrow lanes between Mahatma Gandhi Road and Brabourne Road, a short walk from the Kolkata end of Howrah Bridge. The nearest fire tender, from C R Avenue Fire Station at the Chittaranjan Avenue crossing, needs a window west along MG Road (one-way towards the bridge); a second tender line from the West Bengal Fire & Emergency Services headquarters near Park Street needs a green corridor up Jawaharlal Nehru Road to Esplanade, along Chittaranjan Avenue and MG Road, round the Howrah Bridge end and into Brabourne Road (one-way towards BBD Bag). Once the tenders are in, parked tenders and hose lines take lanes on MG Road and Brabourne Road, a police cordon narrows Strand Road at the lane mouths, handcarts are pushed out onto Chittaranjan Avenue, diverted traffic loads Strand Road north and the afternoon goods traffic queues on Howrah Bridge. The AI proposes each tender window, a goods-vehicle hold on the Howrah Bridge approaches (Howrah City Police at the Howrah end, Kolkata Traffic Police at the Kolkata end), a request to the power utility to isolate supply to the block, and the staged reopening of the cordoned roads; a named officer approves or rejects each, and nothing is sent by itself. Twenty-five minutes in, an ambulance (108) standing by at the east cordon needs a window along MG Road to Kolkata Medical College (no casualty details are modelled). Fire spread, turnout and travel times, lane losses and loads are modelled assumptions, not measurements.

scenarios.name: DVC Release and Howrah Waterlogging — Cross-River Diversion
scenarios.description: SIMULATED. A monsoon weekday morning (Tuesday 14 Sep 2027, 08:45; a scenario, not a forecast and not a record of any real release). Damodar Valley Corporation (DVC) has announced a release from its Maithon and Panchet reservoirs; the release figure in this scenario is a SIMULATED input, not a DVC figure. The scenario assumes that, with the lower Damodar high, steady rain (modelled at 12 mm/h) and a high tide on the Hooghly (MODELLED tide phase), Howrah's drains back up: Grand Trunk Road between Nabanna and Howrah Station goes under water and a bus stalls in it, and water stands on the Howrah Station approach and at the foot of the Nabanna approach to Vidyasagar Setu. On the network Sahoshi models, the only dry way from Nabanna to Howrah Station is across the river twice: over Vidyasagar Setu, along Strand Road past Prinsep Ghat and Babughat, and back over Howrah Bridge, so diverted traffic loads both bridges. A WBSDMA pump-and-relief column runs that diversion behind a Howrah City Police pilot vehicle. The AI proposes the diversion, signal holds on Strand Road, a bus re-routing note for WBTC and a three-language traffic advisory; named officers of Howrah City Police and Kolkata Traffic Police each decide on their side of the river, and nothing is published by itself. Rain, tide, water depth, spread and loads are modelled assumptions.

scenarios.name: Kali Puja Night — Air-Quality Advisory, Kalighat Crowd and Ambulance Priority
scenarios.description: SIMULATED. Kali Puja night (Sunday 8 Nov 2026, 21:30, the Amavasya night; a scenario, not a forecast). Firecrackers across the city push fine-particle pollution up through the evening: the scenario's PM2.5 readings (SIMULATED, not measurements) climb from the Moderately Polluted band at 18:00 to the Very Poor band by 21:00 and touch Severe near midnight, banded indicatively against India's National Air Quality Index (whose bands are defined on 24-hour averages). Devotees fill SP Mukherjee Road around Kalighat temple, flower, lamp and sweet stalls line the road from Hazra to Rashbehari and pandal stalls load Rash Behari Avenue, so traffic slows along the whole stretch. Breathing-difficulty calls rise (modelled as ambulance x1.5). Fifteen minutes in, an ambulance (108) on a breathing-difficulty call needs windows from Tollygunge past Kalighat, Rashbehari and Hazra to Exide crossing, a short run from SSKM Hospital. The AI proposes each window, a priority flag for breathing-difficulty calls and a public health advisory in Bengali, English and Hindi; a named duty officer approves or rejects each, and nothing is published by itself. Crowd loads, readings and speeds are modelled assumptions; no individual is identified.

scenarios.name: Pre-Monsoon Heatwave Afternoon — Overheated Vehicles and Duty Rotations
scenarios.description: SIMULATED. A pre-monsoon heatwave afternoon (Tuesday 27 Apr 2027, 14:00; a scenario, not a forecast). The scenario assumes IMD's heatwave criteria for the plains are met: a SIMULATED maximum of 41.8 °C against a SIMULATED normal of 36.2 °C (departure +5.6 °C; the criteria are a maximum of at least 40 °C with a departure of at least 4.5 °C, or a maximum of at least 45 °C). No real IMD bulletin is quoted. Vehicles overheat: a bus stalls on Vidyasagar Setu, a car with a burst tyre stops on the Maa Flyover, a goods vehicle overheats on EM Bypass between Science City and Chingrighata and a car stalls near Ultadanga (breakdowns modelled at x1.6). Pedestrian flows and street trading thin out in the heat (modelled crowd LOW, market x0.7) and heat-illness calls rise (ambulance x1.3). A Kolkata Traffic Police recovery van runs the corridor from the Nabanna end of Vidyasagar Setu over the AJC Bose Road flyover and the Maa Flyover and up EM Bypass to Ultadanga, clearing each breakdown. The AI proposes where to pre-position recovery vans, shorter duty rotations with shade and water for traffic staff at the most exposed crossings (Esplanade, Park Street, Shyambazar, Ultadanga) and a heat advisory for road users in Bengali, English and Hindi; a named duty officer approves or rejects each. Temperatures, breakdown rates and loads are modelled assumptions.

scenarios.name: Nor'wester Squall — Tree-Falls, Live-Wire Hazard and Staged Reopening
scenarios.description: SIMULATED. A Nor'wester (Kalbaishakhi) evening (Thursday 6 May 2027; a scenario, not a forecast). A squall line crossed the city at about 17:20 with gusts SIMULATED at 70-90 km/h and heavy rain (modelled at 25 mm/h, STORM). At 17:40 the rain lingers and trees are down across the arterials: EM Bypass between Ultadanga and Ruby in three places (a weakened tree falls in a later gust), Red Road along the Maidan, AJC Bose Road between Exide and Moulali, and Rash Behari Avenue, where an overhead wire is also down across the road near Gariahat (live-wire hazard). Signals at Ultadanga are dark after a feeder trips (MODELLED). A KMC tree-clearing crew with a West Bengal Fire & Emergency Services rescue tender, escorted by Kolkata Traffic Police (and the Bidhannagar Police Commissionerate on its stretch), works south along EM Bypass from Ultadanga, so the corridor reopens in stages behind it. The stack may PROPOSE a request to the power utility (and to WBTC if it is a tram overhead line) to isolate the wire on Rash Behari Avenue — a proposal a named duty officer approves or rejects; nothing is sent by itself. Twenty minutes in, an ambulance (108) from Gariahat to Ruby General Hospital needs a window over the Bijon Setu connector. Every reopening is proposed by the AI and decided by a named officer. Gusts, rain, clearance times and loads are modelled assumptions.
